claims.claim: Cyril of Alexandria was Patriarch of Alexandria from 412 to 444.
Cyril of Alexandria was born circa 376 and died in 444.
The work De synagogae defectu is also known as De synagogae defectu seu transnominatione Abrami in Abrahamum (On the Defect of the Synagogue or On the Change of Name from Abram to Abraham).
The work's subtitle indicates it is a demonstration through ancient divine oracles given to the holy patriarchs concerning the exchange and transfer of the Jews and the nations.
The work interprets Abraham's change of name as signifying the triadic number of the divine hypostases (the Trinity).
The work survives in Greek manuscript form, including manuscripts at San Lorenzo de El Escorial (MS Z IV 6 and MS X II 2).
The work is preserved in Migne's Patrologia Graeca.
Cyril of Alexandria was named a doctor of the church in 1882.
Cyril of Alexandria was involved in the expulsion of Jews from Alexandria and opposed Christians whose theology he regarded as contrary to the Nicene faith.
